newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bayer posts 8.3 percent rise in operating profit.
newsitem.headline: Bayer posts 8.3 percent rise in operating profit.

text.p: Bayer AG said Tuesday acquisitions helped boost its profits in the third quarter, leaving the chemical and drug group confident of posting a 10 percent rise in operating earnings.
The company said its third-quarter pre-tax profits climbed 8.3 percent to 981 million marks ($648.3 million) with sales also rising 8.3 percent to 11.747 billion marks ($7.76 billion).

Bayer also said its nine-month pre-tax profits rose 12 percent to 3.7 billion marks ($2.45 billion) while sales grew bby 7.4 percent to 36.54 billion marks ($24.15 billion), broadly in line with forecasts.

Bayer said the sales increase -- which put it on target for a total of 47 billion marks ($31 billion) in 1996 sales -- was largely fuelled by acquisitions of a printing plate business, a fragrance unit and the a plastics unit.
The company also benefited from more favourable exchange rates after the strong mark had largely dented German companies' results last year. Price increases also contributed to the rise in sales.

Management Board Chairman Manfred Schneider said in remarks prepared for a news conference that sales developments were mixed, with foreign sales accounting for most of the growth. Foreign sales rose 10.1 percent in the first nine months while domestic sales climbed only 2.7 percent.

While Bayer said it expected to post a 10 percent rise in operating income for the full year, it also said it expected additional charges in the fourth quarter, due to early retirement, restructuring and other items.
